6. Mr Md. Abdul Haque, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner submits that the enquiry officer after holding the enquiry observing all the legal formalities found the petitioner not guilty of the charges brought against him by the PDB authority and accordingly submitted his report. The respondents without considering the inquiry report inflicted the punishment on the petitioner which is not sustainable in law. He further submits that the respondents did not have any materials in their hands other than the inquiry report to establish the charges against the petitioner and, as such, the impugned order is illegal and has been issued, without lawful authority. Mr. Abdul Haque further submits that in inflicting the punishment upon the petitioner the respondents did not have any independent and different opinion other than the opinion of the enquiry officer and, as such, there was no any basis for inflicting punishment upon the petitioner. The respondents have done it according to their own whims and, as such, the impugned order dated 28-11-2007 is liable to be declared to have been issued without lawful authority and is of no legal effect. He further submits that the punishment has been inflicted upon the petitioner without following the provision of rule 143(4) of the PDB Service Rules 1982, the proceeding was initiated after expiration of specific period of 3(three) months and, as such, the whole proceeding was illegal and, as such, the impugned order is liable to be declared to have been passed without lawful authority. 

 7. Mr Tufailur Rahman, the learned Advocate for the respondent Nos. 2, 3 and 8 submits that the authority has the right to impose any penalty upon an employee for misconduct negligence or for other irregularities considering the inquiry report. In this case the Inquiry report was not satisfactory, after going through the records and considering the facts and circumstances of the case and the inquiry report itself, the respondents inflicted the punishment upon the petitioner because the charges were grave in nature. Mr. Tufailur Rahman further submits that as per rule 143(4) of the PDB Service Rules 1982) the authority has the right to impose any upon any employee for charges of misconduct and irregularities. Considering the reply of the petitioner to the show cause notices, the report of the enquiry officer and the facts and circumstances of the case the authority has imposed the penalty which was justified. However, Mr Tufailur Rahman candidly submits that in the impugned order dated 28-11-2007 it has not been mentioned how the authority was satisfied to impose the penalty upon the petitioner. No reasoning whatsoever was given in the impugned order. 

 11. Rule 143(4) has given an ample power to the authority to impose any penalty upon the person against whom the charges have been brought even ignoring the inquire report. Context of which runs as follows:
